intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Spend an afternoon and evening immersed in the heart of Marrakech's UNESCO-listed medina. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians perform in the square, then wander through the historic souks buying spices, leather goods, and lanterns. With a late Day 1 arrival, skip this on arrival night and begin fresh on Day 2 morning when crowds are manageable and light is ideal for photography. Stay within walking distance by booking a riad inside the medina walls.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Overnight Camp at Erg Chebbi
experiences.description: Journey to the iconic golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga for a 2-night desert experience. Ride camels at sunset into a traditional Berber camp, enjoy a tagine dinner under a sky full of stars, and wake at dawn for a breathtaking sunrise over the dunes. This is the cultural and natural highlight of any Marrakech-Sahara itinerary and worth allocating Days 3–5 to allow travel time and full immersion. Book a camp within the dunes themselves to minimize transfer time.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Explore two of Marrakech's most significant historical landmarks back to back, both located within the southern medina. The 19th-century Bahia Palace dazzles with intricate Moroccan tilework and carved cedar ceilings, while the Saadian Tombs offer a rare glimpse into the royal burial chambers of the 16th-century Saadian dynasty. Combine both in a half-day morning visit to beat the heat and crowds. Staying in a medina riad puts you within a 10-minute walk of both sites.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class with Market Visit
experiences.description: Join a small-group cooking class led by a local chef, beginning with a guided tour of the Mellah spice market to select fresh ingredients. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as chicken bastilla, harira soup, and orange-blossom couscous. Classes typically run 4 hours and include a full sit-down meal. Choose a school located inside or adjacent to the medina to avoid long transfers, especially useful for Days 2 or 6 when you are based in Marrakech.

experiences.name: Aït Benhaddou Kasbah & Draa Valley Day Trip
experiences.description: En route to or from the Sahara on Days 3 or 5, stop at the UNESCO World Heritage ksar of Aït Benhaddou, a stunning fortified mud-brick village used as a backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue through the lush Draa Valley, Morocco's longest river valley, dotted with ancient kasbahs, palm groves, and Berber villages. This route is a natural stop on the Marrakech-to-Merzouga road, eliminating any detour and maximizing your travel days efficiently.
experiences.location: Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Focus on reaching Hotel Aday safely.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a petit taxi (negotiate fare, ~80-100 MAD) or airport bus (Line 19, ~30 MAD) to Hotel Aday at 111 Derb Sidi Bouloukat in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a quick snack from a late-night street stall near Jemaa el-Fna square (open late) — try a msemen flatbread or harira soup for ~10-15 MAD.

day_by_day.notes: Keep small change (MAD) ready for the taxi. Confirm hotel has 24-hour reception. Do not exchange money at the airport — rates are poor. Find a local ATM or bureau de change in the Medina the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, walk 5 minutes to Jemaa el-Fna square to soak in the morning atmosphere — orange juice vendors, snake charmers setting up, and locals going about their day. Then explore the Koutoubia Mosque exterior and gardens (non-Muslims cannot enter, but the exterior and minaret are stunning and free). Stroll through the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) for a taste of Marrakech's layered history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive deep into the Marrakech Souks — the labyrinthine market streets north of Jemaa el-Fna. Explore the spice souk (Rahba Kedima), the dyers' souk, the leather souk, and the metalwork souk. Bargaining is expected — start at 30-40% of the asking price. Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), one of Morocco's most beautiful Islamic schools dating to the 14th century.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna at sunset when the square transforms into a massive open-air food market. Watch the storytellers, musicians, and acrobats. Eat dinner at the square's food stalls — pick a busy stall for freshness and safety.

meals.breakfast: Café de France or a local café near Jemaa el-Fna — mint tea, msemen, and amlou (almond-argan dip) for ~20-30 MAD.
meals.lunch: Cheap local restaurant in the Medina — try a set menu (menu du jour) with harira soup, tagine, and bread for ~40-60 MAD.
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls — merguez sausages, kefta skewers, snail soup (babouche), and fresh-squeezed orange juice for ~50-80 MAD total.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Medina streets are uneven. Keep your bag in front of you in crowded souks. The Ben Youssef Madrasa is best visited early afternoon to avoid tour groups.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917. Arrive early (opens at 9:00 AM) to beat crowds. Afterward, explore the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) — a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on the walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and visit the Lazama Synagogue (small donation appreciated). Browse the antique and second-hand goods in the Mellah market. Then walk to the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a 19th-century palace with ornate Moroccan craftsmanship, painted ceilings, and tranquil courtyards.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the quieter southern Medina streets around Riad Zitoun el-Jedid. Enjoy a relaxed evening walk back toward Jemaa el-Fna. Watch a free outdoor performance at the square — gnawa musicians and Berber storytellers perform nightly.

meals.breakfast: At Hotel Aday if breakfast is included, or a nearby café — café au lait and khobz (Moroccan bread) with olive oil for ~15-25 MAD.
meals.lunch: Restaurant Chez Bahia near the Bahia Palace — local Moroccan set lunch with couscous or tagine for ~50-70 MAD.
meals.dinner: Café Clock Marrakech (Kasbah branch) — try their famous camel burger or vegetarian pastilla for ~60-90 MAD. A cultural hub with live music some evenings.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a combined ticket if available for multiple monuments to save money. The Bahia Palace is most photogenic in the afternoon light. Café Clock often hosts free or low-cost cultural events — check their board.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (6:00-7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert — join a shared budget group tour to Merzouga/Erg Chebbi dunes (approximately 560 km, 9-10 hours). Book through a local agency in the Medina the day before (shared minibus tours cost ~350-500 MAD per person one-way, or ~700-900 MAD for a 2-day shared tour including camel ride and desert camp). En route, pass through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas Mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the journey through the Draa Valley — stop at Aït Benhaddou (UNESCO World Heritage ksar/fortified village, ~30 MAD entry) if the tour includes it. This ancient mud-brick citadel has been used as a film set for Game of Thrones, Gladiator, and Lawrence of Arabia. Continue through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') and the Valley of Roses.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga at sunset. Mount a camel for a 45-60 minute ride into the dunes to your desert camp (included in most budget tours). Watch the spectacular Sahara sunset over the orange dunes. Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner at the camp under a sky full of stars — one of Morocco's most magical experiences.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — grab msemen and mint tea from a street stall near the hotel for ~15-20 MAD.
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route — a simple tagine or sandwich at a local café in the Atlas or Draa Valley for ~40-60 MAD.
meals.dinner: Included in most desert camp packages — traditional Berber meal with tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, and mint tea around a campfire.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara tour 1-2 days in advance from a reputable agency in Marrakech. Compare prices from at least 3 agencies. Bring warm layers — desert nights in March can drop to 5-10°C. Pack a headscarf for sand protection. Charge all devices before leaving Marrakech.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the dunes and watch the Sahara sunrise — an unmissable, breathtaking experience. Take photos, explore the dunes on foot, and enjoy the silence of the desert. After breakfast at camp, ride camels back to the edge of the dunes. Spend the late morning exploring the village of Merzouga — visit local Berber families, see the small lake (Dayet Srji) that attracts flamingos in spring, and browse the small local market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey to Marrakech via shared transport. The route back may vary — some tours return via a different scenic route through the Todra Gorge (dramatic 300m-high limestone canyon, free to enter) or the Dades Valley. Stop for photos and a short walk in the gorge if time permits.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech late evening (around 20:00-21:00). Drop bags at Hotel Aday, freshen up, and take a short walk to Jemaa el-Fna for a late dinner. Reflect on the incredible desert experience.

meals.breakfast: Included at the desert camp — Moroccan bread, olive oil, honey, argan oil, and mint tea.
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant en route — try a hearty lamb or chicken tagine with bread for ~50-70 MAD.
meals.dinner: Back in Marrakech — Jemaa el-Fna food stalls or a cheap Medina restaurant. Try b'stilla (pigeon or chicken pie with almonds and cinnamon) for ~40-60 MAD.

day_by_day.notes: The return journey is long — bring snacks, water, and entertainment. Some budget tours combine Day 4 and 5 as a single overnight trip; confirm your itinerary with the agency. Keep receipts and confirm pickup times clearly.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after the long desert journey. Sleep in, then visit the Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD, or ~200 MAD including the Berber Museum inside) — a stunning botanical garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later owned by Yves Saint Laurent. The electric blue villa and exotic plants are iconic. Visit the adjacent YSL Museum if budget allows (~100 MAD extra) or admire the exterior for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gueliz neighborhood (Marrakech's modern French-built new town) — a contrast to the ancient Medina. Browse the Avenue Mohammed V for local shops, visit the Central Market (Marché Central) for fresh produce, spices, and olives. Head back to the Medina for last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks — argan oil, leather goods, Berber rugs, and spices make great budget gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost hammam experience at a local neighborhood hammam (public hammam costs ~15-20 MAD entry + ~20 MAD for a kessa scrub glove) — a quintessential Moroccan cultural experience. Ask your hotel to recommend the nearest local hammam. End the evening with a final sunset view from a rooftop café terrace overlooking Jemaa el-Fna.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby café — mint tea, amlou, and msemen for ~20-30 MAD.
meals.lunch: Marché Central area in Gueliz — fresh sandwiches, olives, and local pastries for ~30-50 MAD.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last full dinner — try Restaurant Nomad in the Medina (modern Moroccan cuisine, mains ~80-120 MAD) or the classic Café des Épices overlooking the spice square (~70-100 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is very popular — arrive at opening time (9:00 AM) to avoid crowds. The public hammam is a genuine local experience but can be overwhelming for first-timers — ask hotel staff to explain the process beforehand. Bargain hard in the souks today for the best prices.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — take a slow, unhurried walk through the quieter early-morning Medina streets before the crowds arrive. Visit the Mouassine Fountain and the beautiful Mouassine Mosque area (exterior only). Pop into a local bakery (farran) to buy fresh-baked khobz bread straight from the communal oven — a deeply local experience for just 2-3 MAD per loaf.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, visit any missed sights — the Tanneries (best viewed from a leather shop rooftop, free with a small purchase), or simply sit in a café and people-watch. Do final packing at Hotel Aday. Check out and store luggage with the hotel if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport for your departure. Take a petit taxi (~80-100 MAD) or airport bus (~30 MAD). Arrive at least 2 hours before your flight. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, history, desert adventure, and local flavors.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast — visit a local café for a full spread: mint tea, coffee, msemen, beghrir (honeycomb pancakes), honey, and amlou for ~25-35 MAD.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or airport area — a sandwich or pastilla from a local bakery for ~20-40 MAD.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal, or grab a final snack at Jemaa el-Fna before heading to the airport.

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for airport security and check-in at Marrakech Menara Airport, especially on weekends. Use remaining MAD on food, tips, or small souvenirs — MAD is difficult to exchange outside Morocco. Leave a tip for hotel staff (20-30 MAD) as a kind gesture.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-arranged airport transfer or petit taxi (~80–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour hanout (corner shop) close to the hotel in Derb Sidi Bouloukat

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night simple. Confirm your hotel has late check-in arranged. Exchange a small amount of currency (MAD) at the airport for immediate needs. The Medina streets can be confusing at night — share your hotel address in Arabic with your taxi driver.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, begin exploring the heart of the Medina. Visit the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square to soak in the morning atmosphere — orange juice vendors, storytellers, and snake charmers. Then walk to the nearby Koutoubia Mosque (exterior view) and stroll through the surrounding gardens. Head into the souks: explore Souk Semmarine (textiles), Souk des Épices (spice market), and Souk Haddadine (blacksmiths).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (~70 MAD entry) — a stunning 19th-century riad palace with intricate Moroccan tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, walk to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and explore the historic Lazama Synagogue. End the afternoon at the El Badi Palace ruins (~70 MAD entry) for panoramic views and a sense of Marrakech's imperial past.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as the square transforms into a massive open-air food market. Watch the acrobats, musicians, and henna artists. Dine at one of the food stalls (stalls 1–100 are popular) — try harira soup, merguez sandwiches, and fresh-squeezed orange juice.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Aday or a nearby café — traditional Moroccan breakfast with msemen (flatbread), amlou (almond-argan dip), honey, and mint tea (~30–50 MAD)
meals.lunch: Café des Épices near Place Rahba Kedima — rooftop terrace with tagines and sandwiches (~80–120 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls — budget-friendly and authentic (~60–100 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover 5–8 km today. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep a small bag and be mindful of pickpockets in crowded areas. The Medina is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a visit to the Saadian Tombs (~70 MAD entry) — 16th-century royal mausoleums rediscovered in 1917, featuring exquisite mosaic and stucco work. Then head to the Madrasa Ben Youssef (~70 MAD entry), one of the largest Islamic colleges in North Africa, with breathtaking Andalusian-Moroccan architecture. Explore the adjacent Museum of Marrakech (~50 MAD) housed in a 19th-century palace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short taxi ride (~20 MAD) to the Majorelle Garden (~150 MAD entry) — a stunning botanical garden with cobalt-blue buildings designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Visit the adjacent Berber Museum inside the garden. Afterward, explore the Gueliz (Ville Nouvelle) neighborhood for a change of pace — browse art galleries and modern boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Moroccan hammam experience at a mid-range hammam near the Medina such as Hammam Dar el-Bacha (~150–250 MAD for full scrub and steam). Afterward, enjoy a relaxed dinner at a rooftop restaurant in the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Patisserie des Princes near Jemaa el-Fna — fresh pastries, coffee, and Moroccan pancakes (~40–60 MAD)
meals.lunch: Café Arabe in the Medina — Moroccan-Mediterranean fusion in a beautiful riad setting (~120–180 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Le Jardin restaurant in the Medina — set in a lush courtyard garden, serving classic Moroccan dishes like pastilla and lamb tagine (~150–200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Majorelle Garden online in advance — it sells out, especially in spring. The hammam is a quintessential Moroccan experience; bring flip-flops and a change of clothes. March weather in Marrakech is pleasant (~18–24°C), ideal for garden visits.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (~7:00 AM) on a pre-booked shared or private transfer toward the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley route (Ouarzazate → Zagora or Merzouga). The drive to Merzouga (Erg Chebbi dunes) takes approximately 8–9 hours with stops. First stop: the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass through the High Atlas Mountains — dramatic scenery and Berber villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa.' Stop at the Kasbah Taourirt (~30 MAD entry), a UNESCO-listed earthen fortress. Browse the nearby artisan cooperative for handmade carpets and pottery. Continue driving through the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) and the dramatic Draa Valley with its ancient kasbahs and palm groves.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga (~18:00–19:00). Check into a mid-range desert camp or guesthouse (pre-booked). Mount camels for a 45-minute sunset camel trek into the dunes. Watch the sunset over the Sahara — one of Morocco's most iconic experiences. Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner at camp under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Aday before departure — packed or quick (~30–50 MAD)
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside restaurant in Ouarzazate — Moroccan set menu with harira, tagine, and bread (~80–120 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — included in most camp packages; expect couscous, tagine, Berber bread, and mint tea (~150–200 MAD if not included)

day_by_day.notes: Book your desert camp and transport in advance — recommended options near Merzouga include Sahara Desert Camp or similar mid-range camps (~400–700 MAD/night including dinner and breakfast). Bring warm layers — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Pack sunscreen, sunglasses, and a scarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (~6:00 AM) for a magical dawn camel ride or walk to the top of the dunes to watch the sun rise over the Sahara. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast. Explore the village of Merzouga on foot — visit local Gnawa musicians, a fossil shop (the region is rich in trilobite fossils), and interact with nomadic Berber families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional activities near Merzouga: visit the Dayet Srji salt lake (flamingo spotting in spring), take a 4x4 excursion to remote dune areas, or visit the Khamlia village to hear traditional Gnawa music performed by descendants of sub-Saharan slaves. Begin the return journey toward Marrakech via the Todra Gorge route.
day_by_day.evening: Stop and overnight in the Todra Gorge area (Tinghir) — a dramatic canyon with 300-meter-high rose-colored rock walls. Take an evening walk through the gorge as the light turns golden. Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Tinghir.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at the desert camp — included; bread, olive oil, honey, argan oil, eggs, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch or stop at a local café in Merzouga village (~60–80 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at your guesthouse in Tinghir or a local restaurant — try mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) or a vegetable tagine (~100–150 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Todra Gorge is most dramatic in the late afternoon light. The drive from Merzouga to Tinghir is approximately 3–4 hours. If time allows, a short hike into the gorge at dusk is highly recommended. Confirm your guesthouse booking in Tinghir in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning walk through the Todra Gorge before the tourist crowds arrive — the light is spectacular. Continue the drive back toward Marrakech via the Dades Valley (Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs). Stop at the Dades Gorge for photos of the winding road and dramatic rock formations. Visit the Aït Benhaddou UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) — one of Morocco's most photographed sites and a famous film location (~30 MAD entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Aït Benhaddou thoroughly — cross the river on stepping stones, climb to the top of the ksar for panoramic views, and visit local artisan workshops selling pottery and carpets. Continue the final stretch back to Marrakech (~2.5 hours from Aït Benhaddou). Arrive in Marrakech by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hotel Aday, freshen up, and enjoy a final evening in the Medina. Visit the Mellah spice market for last-minute souvenir shopping — saffron, argan oil, ras el hanout spice blend, and rose water are excellent buys. Enjoy a leisurely farewell dinner at a traditional Moroccan restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Tinghir guesthouse — traditional Moroccan spread (~40–60 MAD or included)
meals.lunch: Lunch near Aït Benhaddou at a local restaurant with views of the ksar — tagine and salad (~100–130 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Dar Zitoun or similar mid-range riad restaurant in Marrakech Medina — try a full Moroccan feast: pastilla, lamb tagine with prunes, and bastilla au lait for dessert (~180–250 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Tinghir to Marrakech via Aït Benhaddou is approximately 5–6 hours total with stops. Start early to make the most of Aït Benhaddou. Aït Benhaddou has been used as a filming location for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia — a fascinating cultural and historical stop.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — enjoy a slow breakfast and last walk through the Medina. Visit any missed sites: the Musée de Marrakech, the tanneries (best viewed from leather shop rooftops — free with a guide tip), or simply wander the quieter back alleys of the Medina. Pick up final souvenirs in the souks — leather goods, babouche slippers, lanterns, and Moroccan ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, enjoy a final mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the Medina. Visit the Koutoubia Gardens for a peaceful stroll. If time allows, take a short calèche (horse-drawn carriage) ride around the ramparts of the Medina (~150–200 MAD for 45 minutes). Head to the airport with ample time — allow 1.5–2 hours before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, desert, history, and food across one of the world's most captivating destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday or a nearby café — msemen with honey and argan oil, mint tea (~40–60 MAD)
meals.lunch: Nomad restaurant near the Spice Square — modern Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views (~130–180 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Marrakech Menara Airport is approximately 15–20 minutes from the Medina by taxi (~80–100 MAD). Confirm your departure terminal in advance. Morocco's currency (MAD) cannot be exported in large quantities — spend remaining dirhams or exchange back at the airport. Tipping is customary: 10–15 MAD for small services, 20–50 MAD for guides.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Hotel Aday in the heart of the Medina. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome mint tea ceremony and a light late-night snack prepared by the riad. Settle into your suite and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter at Hotel Aday — traditional Moroccan mezze, olives, fresh bread, and herbal tea arranged by the riad upon request

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer with Hotel Aday in advance. The Medina's narrow derbs (alleyways) require a local guide or driver familiar with the area to reach Derb Sidi Bouloukat. Keep luggage manageable for the final walk to the riad. Rest well — a full day of exploration begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the riad rooftop terrace. Then embark on a guided private walking tour of the Marrakech Medina — explore the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square in the morning calm before the crowds arrive, visit the 16th-century Saadian Tombs (a UNESCO-listed royal necropolis), and stroll through the historic Kasbah neighborhood. Your private guide will provide rich historical context throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the magnificent Bahia Palace — a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan-Andalusian architecture with ornate carved cedar ceilings, zellij tilework, and lush gardens. Afterward, explore the adjacent Mellah (historic Jewish quarter) and its covered souks. Stop at a high-end artisan cooperative to observe master craftsmen working in leather, brass, and mosaic.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitif on the rooftop of a Medina bar with views over the rooftops toward the Koutoubia Minaret at sunset. Dinner at a premium Moroccan restaurant in the Medina — Le Foundouk or Dar Yacout — for a multi-course traditional feast in a beautifully restored riad setting with live Gnawa music.

meals.breakfast: Riad rooftop breakfast — fresh-squeezed orange juice, msemen (Moroccan flatbread), amlou (almond-argan dip), honey, local cheeses, and Moroccan coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant on Derb Aarjan — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with rooftop terrace views; try the lamb pastilla and harira soup
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout or Le Foundouk — 5-course traditional Moroccan dinner including bastilla au pigeon, lamb tagine with preserved lemon, couscous royale, and pastilla au lait for dessert; budget MAD 600–900 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Saadian Tombs tickets in advance as timed entry is required. Reserve dinner at Dar Yacout well ahead — it is one of Marrakech's most celebrated dining experiences. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina's uneven cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Ben Youssef Madrasa — the finest example of Marinid-era Islamic architecture in Morocco, featuring breathtaking stucco carvings, cedar woodwork, and a serene central courtyard. Continue to the Museum of Marrakech housed in a 19th-century palace. Explore the Dyers' Souk (Souk Sabbaghin) and the Spice Market (Rahba Kedima) with your guide explaining the cultural significance of each trade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive private hammam and spa experience at a luxury hammam such as Les Bains de Marrakech or Hammam de la Rose — enjoy a traditional black soap scrub (kessa), ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. This 2–3 hour ritual is a cornerstone of Moroccan culture and the perfect afternoon indulgence.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the rooftop bar of La Mamounia Hotel (non-guest access available at the bar) — one of the world's great luxury hotels with legendary gardens and Art Deco-Moorish interiors. Dinner at Comptoir Darna — a glamorous Marrakech institution blending Moroccan and French cuisine with live belly dancing performances.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast — beghrir (semolina pancakes with honey and butter), fresh fruit platter, Moroccan mint tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café des Épices overlooking Rahba Kedima square — Moroccan salads, kefta brochettes, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Comptoir Darna — duck pastilla, sea bass chermoula, and chocolate fondant with orange blossom cream; vibrant atmosphere with live entertainment; budget MAD 700–1,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam session at least 2 days in advance. Bring a change of comfortable clothing for after the hammam. La Mamounia bar requires smart-casual dress code. The hammam experience typically lasts 2–3 hours — plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the scenic drive toward the Sahara Desert via the dramatic Draa Valley and Dades Gorges. Stop at the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas for panoramic views and photos. Visit the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou — a stunning fortified ksar (village) that has served as a backdrop for films including Lawrence of Arabia and Game of Thrones. Guided walk through the ancient earthen citadel with a local expert.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving through the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) near Kelaat M'Gouna — in mid-March the rose bushes are beginning to bloom. Stop at a local cooperative to learn about rose water and argan oil production. Pass through the dramatic Todra Gorge for a short walk between the towering 300-meter canyon walls. Continue toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your luxury desert camp near Merzouga as the sun sets over the Erg Chebbi dunes. Mount camels for a guided sunset camel trek into the dunes — watch the Sahara turn gold, amber, and crimson. Arrive at your exclusive private luxury camp (such as Scarabeo Camp or Erg Chebbi Luxury Camp) for a candlelit dinner under a sky blazing with stars, accompanied by traditional Berber music around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the riad before departure — packed premium breakfast box if departing before 7:00am
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional restaurant in Aït Benhaddou village — Berber tagine, fresh salads, and mint tea with views of the ksar
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the luxury desert camp — Berber-spiced lamb mechoui, vegetable couscous, Moroccan salad spread, and traditional sweets; mint tea and dates by the campfire

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (approximately 8–9 hours total with stops) — depart by 7:00–7:30am. Ensure your private driver is confirmed the night before. Pack a light jacket as the Atlas Mountains and desert nights can be cold in March (temperatures can drop to 5–10°C). Bring a scarf for the camel ride. Charge all devices before leaving Marrakech as charging options are limited in the desert.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a private guided sunrise hike to the top of the Erg Chebbi dunes — one of the most spectacular experiences in all of Morocco. Watch the Sahara come alive in the early morning light with shifting colors across the sand sea. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast. Explore the edge of the dunes on foot or by 4x4 sandboarding excursion. Visit a local Berber nomad family encampment for authentic tea and conversation about desert life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the village of Merzouga and the Gnawa musicians' quarter — learn about the ancient spiritual music tradition of the Saharan Gnawa people. Optional quad biking or 4x4 dune bashing across the Erg Chebbi for an adrenaline experience. Relax at the camp with a traditional hammam tent treatment before departure. Begin the return journey toward Ouarzazate, stopping at the Draa Valley oasis palmeries.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight in Ouarzazate — the 'Gateway to the Sahara' and Morocco's film capital. Check into a luxury kasbah hotel such as Dar Kamar or Le Berbère Palace. Dinner at the hotel restaurant or at a local fine dining establishment featuring southern Moroccan cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Berber camp breakfast — msemen, honey, argan oil, hard-boiled eggs, fresh fruit, and Berber coffee (spiced with cardamom and ginger)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Merzouga restaurant or at the camp — camel meat tagine (a regional specialty), Berber pizza (madfouna), and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Kamar in Ouarzazate — refined southern Moroccan cuisine in a beautifully restored kasbah setting; lamb with prunes and almonds, chicken with preserved lemon and olives

day_by_day.notes: Set an alarm for 5:30am to catch the sunrise — it is absolutely worth it. The dune hike takes approximately 30–45 minutes each way. Wear closed shoes for the sand. Confirm the return vehicle and Ouarzazate hotel booking before leaving Marrakech. March nights in the desert are cold — the luxury camp will provide blankets and heating.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Taourirt Kasbah in Ouarzazate — a magnificent 19th-century earthen fortress and UNESCO-listed site, once the seat of the powerful Glaoui clan. Guided tour of the kasbah's labyrinthine interior, painted chambers, and rooftop terraces with panoramic views. Visit the adjacent Atlas Film Studios — the largest film studios in the world outside Hollywood, where Gladiator, The Mummy, and Babel were filmed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive back toward Marrakech via the Tizi n'Tichka pass. Stop at a Berber village in the High Atlas for a home-hosted lunch experience — a rare and intimate glimpse into mountain Berber family life. Continue to Marrakech, arriving in the late afternoon. Check back into Hotel Aday and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Marrakech — return to Djemaa el-Fna square at dusk to experience the full spectacle: snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and dozens of open-air food stalls filling the square with smoke and aromas. Splurge on a farewell dinner at La Grande Table Marocaine inside La Mamounia Hotel — the pinnacle of Moroccan fine dining with impeccable service and an extraordinary wine list.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Ouarzazate hotel — continental and Moroccan spread with fresh pastries, local honey, and coffee
meals.lunch: Home-hosted Berber lunch in a High Atlas village — slow-cooked lamb tagine, fresh bread baked in a clay oven, seasonal vegetables, and mint tea; an authentic and unforgettable experience
meals.dinner: La Grande Table Marocaine at La Mamounia — 7-course tasting menu featuring the finest Moroccan ingredients prepared with French technique; wine pairing available; budget MAD 1,200–1,800 per person; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Book La Grande Table Marocaine at La Mamounia as early as possible — it is one of the most sought-after reservations in Marrakech. Smart dress code required (no shorts or sandals). The home-hosted lunch in the Atlas can be arranged through your private guide or the hotel concierge — confirm 48 hours in advance. Allow extra time for the mountain pass drive as road conditions can vary.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning in Marrakech. Last rooftop breakfast at Hotel Aday savoring the Medina rooftops and the call to prayer. Spend the morning on a curated luxury shopping experience in the souks with a personal guide — visit master artisans for bespoke leather goods, hand-knotted Berber rugs, silver jewelry, and argan oil products. Your guide will help negotiate fair prices and identify authentic quality pieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — visit the Majorelle Garden and the adjacent Yves Saint Laurent Museum (Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech) for a final cultural experience. The cobalt-blue garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by YSL is one of Marrakech's most beautiful spaces. Enjoy a final mint tea at the garden café. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. Carry the memories of the Sahara stars, the call to prayer over the Medina, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast — full Moroccan spread with all favorites from the week: msemen, beghrir, amlou, fresh orange juice, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Bousafsaf near the Majorelle Garden — light Moroccan fare, salads, and fresh juices in a relaxed garden setting
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining — consider purchasing a box of premium Moroccan pastries (cornes de gazelle, fekkas, chebakia) from a Medina patisserie as a farewell treat and gift

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for the airport transfer and check-in — Marrakech Menara Airport can be busy. Confirm checkout time with Hotel Aday and arrange luggage storage if needed for afternoon activities. Purchase any last-minute souvenirs at the airport duty-free for convenience. Declare any argan oil or food products at customs if returning to the US.

query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March
